messages:
maya: Heads-up — ran a quick replay QA on yesterday's prod traces to validate a suspected perf regression after the kernel selection change. initial run shows ~12% tail-latency regression for long-context (>2048) requests :eyes:
liam: ugh. which kernel switch? the dynamic-matmul branch?
maya: yeah, dynamic-matmul v2 fallback path. hypothesis: batching heuristics + kv warmup compounding the kernel switch costs. also noticed non-deterministic of a tiny subset of traces.
olivia: can you share the exact replay command you used? want to reproduce locally.
maya: command pasted below:
```
./replay-harness --traces=prod/2026-03-16.slice --sample=cohort:longctx=0.5,shortctx=0.2 --anon=hash --seed=42 --model=redwood/open-13b:2026-03-10 --kernels=dynamic-matmul-v2,matmul-v1 --kv-warmup=true --workers=32 --stream=false
```
sam: quick QA notes: anonymization used SHA256-hash pseudoids (no plaintext PII), we also scrubbed user-agent strings and dropped request bodies > 2KB. double-check that the anon step didn't alter tokenization boundaries (it shouldn't but worth confirming).
jordan: for apples-to-apples we need to lock: model hash, tokenizer version, kernel selection list order, batching policy, and system load. otherwise apples->oranges.
liam: agree. also record env: TF_CPP_MIN_LOG_LEVEL, OMP_NUM_THREADS, CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES. tiny env diffs changed kernel choice heuristics for us before.
maya: good call. I re-ran with exact env snapshot and pinned kernel order (force v1 first then v2) — parity improved but still 6% tail gap. profiling shows increased time in "matmul_dispatcher::choose_kernel" and "kv_cache::lookup_miss_path".
replay-bot: analysis finished: parity-check failed 6.1% of traces (tail latency > baseline), deterministic-check failed for 0.9% of traces. logs: s3://redwood-replay/artifacts/2139001234/summary.json
olivia: can you attach a small reproducer (1k traces) we can run on dev GPUs? CI won't run whole set.
maya: uploading subset now. link: s3://redwood-replay/artifacts/2139001234/samples/longctx-1k.tar.gz
sam: for determinism, try setting REPLAY_DETERMINISTIC=1 and RNG_SEED=42 and run with single worker to rule out racey kv warmup. if that fixes it, we can bisect parallelism heuristics.
liam: i'll run that tomorrow morning. also add a run with continuous batching disabled: --disable-continuous-batching to see if batching heuristics amplify the kernel overhead.
jordan: what about KV cache warmup policy? if warmup populates different KV sizes, kernel choice could flip. we should capture KV hit-rate and mean chain length per request.
maya: added debug counters and a small perf snippet from the failing run:
```
Top hot functions:
  matmul_kernel_v2_main         34.2%
  matmul_dispatcher::choose    12.8%
  kv_cache::lookup_miss_path   9.6%
  softmax_opt                  6.1%
```
olivia: 34% in v2 is significant. could be a slower kernel on these shapes. suggest we run kernel microbenchmarks for the long-context shapes (seq_len 4096, batch 1..8) and compare GFLOPS.
liam: i'll kick off microbenchmarks and a 3x replay: baseline (matmul-v1 only), v2-only, and mixed with our batching policy. results will be in the same artifact prefix.
maya: action items then:
- liam: microbench + replay triage (baseline / v2-only / mixed) — attach perf counters and kernel GFLOPS
- liam & sam: determinism runs with REPLAY_DETERMINISTIC=1 and single-worker reproducer
- olivia: confirm anonymization did not change token boundaries on sample set
- jordan: add KV hit/miss tracer to replay artifacts and histogram by cohort
- maya: run parity diff and produce minimal trace list triggering regression

liam: got it. I'll post status in this thread and ping if I need a dev GPU. :thumbsup:
maya: thanks — let's aim to close this by EOD tomorrow. if we find a kernel perf regression, we may need a rollback or temporary routing policy to prefer v1 for long-context until kernel is fixed.
tracebot: scheduled deterministic replays (1k subset) to run at 2026-03-18T09:00Z. artifacts will be uploaded to s3 when done.
